title: DR1 tells the user each document can be up to 50MB; the frontend tells the user 10 MB and rejects anything larger.

finding.frontend: The first bullet under "Your file must be:" reads "smaller than 10 MB" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:43-48). The number is not decoration: a file over 10,000,000 bytes is refused with "The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB", and the route's own payload cap is set just above it so an oversize post is caught rather than dropped (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-49). The comment beside the constant records why it is 10 and not more — it is set to stay clear of the CDP nginx ingress cap, not chosen as a policy (:40-41).
finding.prototype: The requirements list under Attachment opens with "files that are smaller than 50MB" (app/views/upload-documents.html:166), visible on dr1-upload-documents and repeated in every error state of the page.
finding.difference: Raise the per-file limit to 50MB and change the bullet to match. This cannot land in the frontend alone: the 10 MB figure exists because the platform ingress rejects a larger body before the application sees it, so the ingress limit has to be raised on the deployed environments first, then MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB and MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, then the bullet and the oversize message. Settle the unit at the same time — DR1 writes "50MB" with no space and the frontend writes "10 MB" with one.
finding.falsifiedBy: Uploading a 20MB document through the frontend and having it save.

relatedTo.why: both limits are stated in the same four-bullet requirements list
